issues.title: parser: parseRows turns an empty line into a row with one empty field
issues.body: `parseRows` in `src/parser/read.ts` turns an empty line into a row with one empty field, so a text that ends with a line break gets an empty last row. Done when `parseRows` gives no row for an empty line.

issues.title: parser: parseRows reads a tab as a field separator
issues.body: `parseRows` in `src/parser/read.ts` splits a line at a tab too, so a field that holds a tab becomes two fields. `parseRows` must split a line only at commas.

issues.title: parser: parseRows and importTable do not split a text with lone CR line ends
issues.body:
Both readers split lines at `/\r?\n/` (`src/parser/read.ts:59`, `src/import-table.ts:6`). A text with lone `\r` line ends (classic Mac) stays one line: `parseRows('a,b\rc,d')` gives `[["a","b\rc","d"]]`, not two rows.

Found in the review of the fix for #91. Out of scope there: #91 is about empty lines, and the old code did not split at a lone CR either.

issues.title: parser: a quoted field with a line break is split into two rows
issues.body:
Both readers split the text into lines before they read quotes (`src/parser/read.ts:59`, `src/import-table.ts:6`). A quoted value that holds a line break becomes two broken rows: `parseRows('"x\ny",b')` gives `[["\"x"],["y\"","b"]]`, not `[["x\ny","b"]]`. Since #91, an empty line inside such a value is dropped too.

Found in the review of the fix for #91. Out of scope there: the fix needs a reader that knows quotes, not a line split.

issues.title: parser: parseRows keeps a UTF-8 BOM in the first field
issues.body:
`parseRows` in `src/parser/read.ts` does not remove a leading `﻿`. CSV exports from Windows often start with one. `parseRows('﻿"id",name')` gives `[["﻿\"id\"","name"]]`: the first header keeps the BOM and its quotes. `importTable` acts the same.

Found in the review of the fix for #91. Out of scope there.

issues.title: parser: importTable and parseRows are two CSV readers that give different rows
issues.body:
`importTable` in `src/import-table.ts` reads CSV with `splitLine` (`src/parser/split.ts`). It does not use `parseRows` (`src/parser/read.ts`). The two readers give different rows:

- `importTable` does not unquote: `importTable('a,"x,y"')` gives `[["a","\"x","y\""]]`.
- `splitLine` drops an empty last field: `importTable('a,b,\nc,d,e')` gives rows of 2 and 3 fields. `parseRows` keeps the empty field.

The fix for #91 had to put the same line split and empty-line filter in both readers. Each later fix to line ends or quotes must be made twice. `importTable` can call `parseRows`, or both can share one line reader in `src/parser/`.

Found in the review of the fix for #91. Out of scope there: it changes what `importTable` returns.

issues.title: docs: the install command in the README has a typo
issues.body:
`README.md:3` says `npm instal shop`. npm has no `instal` command, so the command fails. It must be `npm install shop`.

Found in the review of the fix for #91. Out of scope there: the README is outside `src/parser/`.
